base.name: Catan (Base Game)
base.descriptionTitle: 🏜️ Welcome to the Island of Broken Friendships
base.description: The classic Settlers of Catan — where you'll learn that your closest friends will happily blockade your only road for a single piece of wheat. Collect resources, build roads, settlements and cities, trade with increasingly hostile neighbors, and desperately race to 10 Victory Points before someone drops a Monopoly card on you. Simple rules, infinite grudges.

cards.name: Lumber
cards.description: Produced by Forest hexes when their number is rolled.
usages: Build a Road (Lumber + Brick)
Build a Settlement (Lumber + Brick + Wool + Grain)

cards.name: Brick
cards.description: Produced by Hills hexes when their number is rolled.
usages: Build a Road (Lumber + Brick)
Build a Settlement (Lumber + Brick + Wool + Grain)

cards.name: Wool
cards.description: Produced by Pasture hexes when their number is rolled.
usages: Build a Settlement (Lumber + Brick + Wool + Grain)
Build a City (× in City cost)
Buy a Development Card (Ore + Grain + Wool)

cards.name: Grain
cards.description: Produced by Fields hexes when their number is rolled.
usages: Build a Settlement (Lumber + Brick + Wool + Grain)
Upgrade to City (Ore×3 + Grain×2)
Buy a Development Card (Ore + Grain + Wool)

cards.name: Ore
cards.description: Produced by Mountain hexes when their number is rolled.
usages: Upgrade to City (Ore×3 + Grain×2)
Buy a Development Card (Ore + Grain + Wool)

cards.name: Knight

Collect Largest Army card when you play 3 knights (2 VP)

Compete for Longest Road (2 VP when ≥5 roads)

cards.name: Year of Plenty (Invention)

usages: Grab the exact resources you need to build
Complete a combination you're one resource short on

cards.name: Monopoly

usages: Disrupt an opponent on the verge of a big build
Collect a resource you urgently need

cards.name: Chapel

Play all at once to surprise opponents when claiming victory

cards.name: Great Hall
cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. Kept secret until you reveal it to win (or until the game ends).
usages: Count towards 10 VP to win
Play all at once to surprise opponents when claiming victory

cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. Kept secret until you reveal it to win (or until the game ends).
usages: Count towards 10 VP to win
Play all at once to surprise opponents when claiming victory

cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. Kept secret until you reveal it to win (or until the game ends).
usages: Count towards 10 VP to win
Play all at once to surprise opponents when claiming victory

cards.name: University
cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. Kept secret until you reveal it to win (or until the game ends).
usages: Count towards 10 VP to win
Play all at once to surprise opponents when claiming victory

cards.name: Longest Road (Longest Route)
cards.description: Awarded to the first player with a continuous road of 5+ segments. Worth 2 Victory Points. Another player can steal it by building a longer road.
usages: Build roads aggressively to claim the card
Break an opponent's road by placing a settlement in the middle

cards.name: Largest Army
cards.description: Awarded to the first player who plays 3 Knight cards. Worth 2 Victory Points. Another player can steal it by playing more Knights.
usages: Play Knights to control the Robber and earn 2 VP
Protect wheat/ore hexes from the Robber

cards.name: Building Cost Card
cards.description: Reference card showing all construction costs in Catan.
usages: Road: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick
Settlement: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick + 1 Wool + 1 Grain
City: 3 Ore + 2 Grain
Development Card: 1 Ore + 1 Grain + 1 Wool

setup: Assemble the sea frame, place 19 terrain hexes and number discs inside.
Sort resource cards into 5 stacks; shuffle development cards facedown.
Place the Robber on the desert hex.
Each player places 2 settlements and 2 roads (round 1 clockwise, round 2 reverse).
Collect starting resources from hexes adjacent to your second settlement.

turnOverview.title: 1. Production Phase
turnOverview.detail: Optionally play a development card, then roll both dice. All players collect resources from hexes matching the roll. On a 7: players with >7 cards discard half, then move the Robber and steal.

turnOverview.title: 2. Action Phase
turnOverview.detail: Trade with players or the supply (4:1, 3:1, or 2:1 via ports). Build roads, settlements, cities, or buy development cards. Play 1 development card if you didn't before the roll.

keyRules.title: Roads
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick. Must connect to your existing network. Max 15 per player. Worth 0 VP.

keyRules.title: Settlements
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick + 1 Wool + 1 Grain. Must obey distance rule (2 edges from any building). Max 5 per player. Worth 1 VP.

keyRules.title: Cities
keyRules.detail: Cost: 3 Ore + 2 Grain. Upgrade a settlement (produces 2 resources). Max 4 per player. Worth 2 VP.

keyRules.title: Development Cards
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Ore + 1 Grain + 1 Wool. Types: Knight (14), Road Building (2), Year of Plenty (2), Monopoly (2), VP cards (5). Cannot play on the turn bought.

keyRules.title: Longest Road
keyRules.detail: First player with 5+ continuous roads gets this tile (2 VP). Can be stolen if another player builds longer.

keyRules.title: Largest Army
keyRules.detail: First player to play 3 Knights gets this tile (2 VP). Can be stolen by playing more.

keyRules.title: Robber (rolling a 7)
keyRules.detail: Players with >7 cards discard half. Active player moves the Robber to a new hex and steals 1 random card from an adjacent player.

keyRules.title: Trading
keyRules.detail: On your turn: trade freely with other players, or trade with the supply at 4:1 (general), 3:1 (any port), or 2:1 (specific port).

scenarios.name: Fixed Setup
scenarios.description: Pre-determined hex and number layout for beginners.
details: Terrain hexes and numbers placed as shown in rulebook
Recommended for first-time players

scenarios.name: Variable Setup
scenarios.description: Randomized board for experienced players.
details: Shuffle sea frame pieces and terrain hexes
Place number discs alphabetically counterclockwise, skip the desert
Players place settlements in two rounds (clockwise then reverse)

buildingCosts.name: Road
buildingCosts.note: Must connect to your network. Max 15 per player.

buildingCosts.name: Settlement
buildingCosts.note: Respect the 2-edge distance rule. Max 5 per player.

buildingCosts.name: City
buildingCosts.note: Upgrades a settlement; produces 2 resources per roll. Max 4 per player.

buildingCosts.name: Development Card
buildingCosts.note: Cannot be played on the turn bought (except VP cards on a winning turn).

trading.title: Bank
trading.detail: Any 4 identical resources for 1 of your choice, anytime on your turn.

trading.title: Generic Harbour
trading.detail: Build a settlement/city on a 3:1 port to trade any 3 identical resources for 1.

trading.title: Specific Harbour
trading.detail: Five resource-specific ports let you swap 2 of that resource for 1 of anything.

trading.title: Player Trade
trading.detail: Negotiate freely with other players during your turn — rates are whatever you can convince them to accept.

reference.tradingNote: You can only trade during your own Action phase — that is, after you roll and collect resources, never before the roll.

turnFlow.title: Play a dev card (optional)
turnFlow.detail: May be played before rolling if bought on a prior turn.

turnFlow.title: Roll the dice
turnFlow.detail: Sum of both dice determines which hexes produce this turn.

turnFlow.title: Production
turnFlow.detail: Each player collects resources from their settlements (×1) and cities (×2) adjacent to a producing hex.

turnFlow.title: On a 7: Robber
turnFlow.detail: Players with >7 cards discard half (rounded down). Active player moves the robber and steals 1 random card.

turnFlow.title: Trade
turnFlow.detail: Trade with other players, or with the bank/ports at 4:1 / 3:1 / 2:1.

turnFlow.title: Build
turnFlow.detail: Spend resources on roads, settlements, cities, or development cards.

turnFlow.title: Pass
turnFlow.detail: End your turn by passing the dice to the player on your left.

beginner.title: Count the pips, not the numbers
beginner.body: Each number token has small red dots (pips) equal to how many ways it rolls on 2d6. A 6 or 8 is 5 pips; a 2 or 12 is 1 pip. Score a candidate spot by summing its pips — higher is better.

beginner.title: Cover all five resources
beginner.body: With your two starting settlements, aim to touch all five resource types. Missing one forces expensive bank trades (4:1) and slows every build in the midgame.

beginner.title: Wood + brick = early expansion
beginner.body: Roads and settlements both cost wood and brick. A strong first-turn settlement usually sits on decent wood and brick so you can race to a third settlement before the wheat/ore phase begins.

beginner.title: Ports are good, not great
beginner.body: A 2:1 port on a resource you massively over-produce is excellent; a port without the matching production is a VP you could have used on a resource settlement instead.

beginner.title: Dev cards are not free points
beginner.body: Only 5 of ~25 dev cards are VPs. Buy development cards because you want Knights for Largest Army or flexibility — treat the VPs as a bonus, not a plan.

intermediate.title: Commit to Longest Road, or don't
intermediate.body: Longest Road is 2 VP but needs 5+ segments and is vulnerable to a disrupting settlement. Either commit early (wood/brick-heavy start) or skip it entirely — half-investing loses you resources AND the VP.

intermediate.title: Largest Army is cheaper than it looks
intermediate.body: 3 Knights = 2 VP plus ongoing robber control. If your opponents have no knight pressure, you can often claim it uncontested for what amounts to 6 dev-card buys.

intermediate.title: Robber the leader, not the nearest
intermediate.body: The robber is a political weapon. Move it onto the hex producing the most for whoever is closest to winning, not the hex nearest to you. Target the score leader's best production — you'll get repaid in goodwill.

intermediate.title: Anchor high, accept the second offer
intermediate.body: Open trades at rates worse than 1:1. Opponents compare to your anchor, not to the 4:1 bank. You'll often land a 2:1 player trade simply because it looks generous next to your first ask.

intermediate.title: Sometimes the best play is a blocking road
intermediate.body: A road you will never extend can still be worth building if it walls off an opponent's only expansion lane. Cost-benefit: 1 wood + 1 brick vs. denying your rival a 10-pip settlement.

advanced.title: Chase expected value, not variance
advanced.body: Two 4-pip hexes produce the same long-run total as one 8-pip hex, but with less variance — fewer empty turns. For consistent builds, prefer spreading across 3-4 medium numbers over stacking two hot numbers.

advanced.title: Track opponent hands
advanced.body: After each roll, note who collects what. When an opponent has clearly not drawn wheat for 8 rolls, a wheat Monopoly nets you 6-8 cards from the other players instead — retarget on the fly.

advanced.title: Threaten two cities at once
advanced.body: In the endgame, keep 8+ resources that could buy a city upgrade on either of two settlements. Opponents can only robber one — your next turn still builds.

advanced.title: Avoid kingmaker math in 4p
advanced.body: If you can't win this turn, don't hand a free trade to the player about to. Ratio-fair trades with the second-place player are always better than charity to the leader — even if it means you pay 4:1 to the bank.

seafarers.name: Catan: Seafarers
seafarers.descriptionTitle: ⛵ Because One Island Wasn't Enough Drama
seafarers.description: Explore an archipelago of islands because apparently ruining friendships on a single landmass wasn't satisfying enough. Build ships to sail the seas, discover new islands with gold fields (that everyone will immediately fight over), and settle distant shores for bonus VP. Now your road-blocking nemesis can follow you across the ocean.

cards.name: Ship
cards.description: Ships extend your trade routes across water hexes. They work like roads on the sea.
usages: Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Wool
Can be moved (the end ship of an open route) once per turn
Max 15 ships per player
Placed on a sea edge touching a settlement/city or another ship you own
Counts toward Longest Trade Route (Longest Route)
A ship cannot be moved on the turn it was built

cards.name: Gold Field
cards.description: Special hex that produces a wild resource. When its number is rolled, adjacent players choose any resource they want from the bank.
usages: Highly valuable — worth settling early
Each adjacent settlement yields 1 free resource of choice
Each adjacent city yields 2 free resources of choice (any mix)

cards.name: Warship
cards.description: The Pirate Islands scenario only. Reveal a Knight card to turn one normal ship of your route into a warship (lay it on its side).
usages: Converts the normal ship closest to your route's starting settlement
4 players: Victory Point cards also count as Knights
Your warship count is your strength against pirate attacks and your fortress

cards.name: New Island Bonus
cards.description: In most Seafarers scenarios, placing your first settlement on a new island earns you bonus Victory Points (usually 2, sometimes 1).
usages: Plan ship routes to reach distant islands quickly
Multiple players can earn VP from the same island

cards.name: Pirate
cards.description: The Pirate is added alongside the Robber in Seafarers (both stay in play). Move it to any sea hex to block ships. Steal from an adjacent player with a ship there.
usages: Activated by rolling a 7 or playing a Knight
No ship may be built on, or moved to/from, an edge of its hex

cards.name: Pirate Fortress
cards.description: The Pirate Islands scenario only. Each player has a fortress in their colour on the western islands (a settlement on 3 tokens). You must capture yours to win.
usages: When your ship route reaches it, attack at the end of your turn: roll 1 die
More warships than the roll: remove 1 of its 3 tokens. Tie: lose 1 ship. Fewer: lose 2 ships
Your turn ends after an attack (max 1 attack per turn)
All 3 tokens gone: it becomes your settlement (1 VP, produces, can become a city)

cards.name: Wonder
cards.description: The Wonders of Catan scenario only. Meet a Wonder's requirement, claim it, then build its 4 levels.
usages: 5 Wonders, each with its own start requirement (e.g. a city at a port + 5+ consecutive, unbranched roads/ships)
Only 1 Wonder per player; once claimed, no one else may build it
Each level costs the same 5 resources; build as many levels per turn as you can afford
Win by completing level 4, OR at 10+ VP with a higher Wonder level than everyone else

cards.name: Village
cards.description: Cloth for Catan scenario only. The number discs on the 4 small islands are villages, each starting with 5 cloth tokens. No one may build settlements on those islands.
usages: Connect a ship route from your settlement/city to a village: take 1 cloth at once
Whenever its number is rolled, every player connected to it takes 1 cloth
A route to a village is closed: its ships can't be moved
An empty village stops producing cloth

cards.name: Cloth Token
cards.description: Cloth for Catan scenario only. Earned from villages; collect pairs for VP.
usages: 2 cloth tokens = 1 VP; an unpaired token is worth nothing
You can't move the Pirate until you have a route to a village; after that, the Pirate may steal a cloth token instead of a resource
The game also ends when 5+ of the 8 villages are empty (most VP wins; tie: most cloth)

setup: Uses a special Seafarers sea frame with multiple islands.
Place terrain hexes, sea hexes, and gold field hexes per scenario map.
Each player receives 15 ships in addition to standard pieces.
Robber and Pirate start where the scenario says (Pirate Islands has no Robber; Wonders of Catan has no Pirate).
Starting settlements follow the scenario (some must go on the main island). A coastal starting settlement may take a ship instead of a road.

turnOverview.title: Production & Action
turnOverview.detail: Same as base game, but ships can be built and moved. On a 7, choose to move the Robber OR the Pirate.

turnOverview.title: Ship Movement
turnOverview.detail: Once per turn, move 1 ship that has an open end (not connected on both sides) to a new legal position. Not a ship built this turn, or one in a closed route between two of your buildings.

keyRules.title: Ships
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Wool. Placed on sea hex edges. Count toward Longest Route. Cannot move on the turn built.

keyRules.title: Gold Fields
keyRules.detail: When the number is rolled, each adjacent player chooses any 1 resource (2 for a city).

keyRules.title: Pirate
keyRules.detail: Move to any sea hex. Steal 1 resource from a player with a ship there. Blocks ship placement/movement.

keyRules.title: Longest Trade Route (Longest Route)
keyRules.detail: Roads and ships combine into a route, but only connect through your own buildings (settlements/cities).

keyRules.title: Road Building card
keyRules.detail: Can build 2 roads, 2 ships, or 1 of each.

keyRules.title: Knight card
keyRules.detail: Lets you move the Robber OR the Pirate.

keyRules.title: New-Island Bonus
keyRules.detail: In scenarios with this bonus, your first settlement on each new island (or region) earns +2 VP (+1 in Wonders of Catan and New World), even if others settled there first. The VP tokens go under that settlement.

scenarios.name: Heading for New Shores
scenarios.description: Settle small islands across the sea.
details: +2 VP for first settlement on each small island

scenarios.name: The Four Islands
scenarios.description: Four separate islands to colonize.
details: +2 VP for first settlement on each unexplored island

scenarios.name: The Fog Islands
scenarios.description: Facedown hexes revealed when you build adjacent.
details: A road/ship next to an empty space reveals the next hex: land → take 1 of its resource; sea → nothing
Unknown terrain adds exploration challenge

scenarios.name: Through the Desert
scenarios.description: A desert divides the island into regions.
details: +2 VP for first settlement in each unexplored region

scenarios.name: The Forgotten Tribe
scenarios.description: Sail ships to special edges to collect VP tokens, dev cards, and ports.
details: Build a ship onto an edge with a VP token (1 VP each), dev card, or port to claim it
Settlements only allowed on hexes with a number disc

scenarios.name: Cloth for Catan
scenarios.description: Cloth tokens from village trade routes.
details: Game can also end when 5+ villages are empty
Steal cloth or resources via pirate
Connect a ship route to a village: 1 cloth now, +1 whenever its number is rolled
2 cloth tokens = 1 VP

scenarios.name: The Pirate Islands
scenarios.description: Build warships and conquer pirate fortresses.
details: Knight cards convert ships to warships
No Longest Route/Largest Army tiles
Each player has their own pirate fortress
Attack your fortress: roll 1 die; more warships than the roll removes 1 of its 3 tokens

scenarios.name: The Wonders of Catan
scenarios.description: Claim and build one of 5 Wonders to win.
details: 4 levels, each costs 5 resources
Complete your Wonder OR reach 10+ VP with highest wonder level
Each Wonder has its own requirement to start
Claimed Wonders are exclusive

scenarios.name: New World
scenarios.description: Fully randomized island layout.
details: +1 VP for first settlement on each unexplored island
Hexes are placed at random; players take turns placing the ports

reference.tradingNote: Seafarers keeps base-game trading ratios — no new trade rules, but coastal ports remain exceptionally strong when shipping routes connect them.

buildingCosts.name: Road
buildingCosts.note: Max 15 per player. Can't share a coastal edge with a ship; links to ships only at your settlement/city.

buildingCosts.name: Ship
buildingCosts.note: Max 15 per player. You may move 1 open-end ship per turn.

buildingCosts.name: Settlement
buildingCosts.note: Distance rule applies on every island. Max 5 per player. Your first on a new island may earn bonus VP (scenario rules).

buildingCosts.name: City
buildingCosts.note: Upgrades a settlement. Produces 2 per hex; 2 of your choice from a gold field. Max 4 per player.

buildingCosts.name: Development Card
buildingCosts.note: Knight moves the Robber OR the Pirate; Road Building can place ships too.

turnFlow.title: Play a dev card (optional)
turnFlow.detail: Dev cards bought on a previous turn. Knight lets you move Robber OR Pirate.

turnFlow.title: Roll the dice
turnFlow.detail: Hexes produce as normal; gold fields give any resource of choice (1 per settlement, 2 per city).

turnFlow.title: On a 7: Robber or Pirate
turnFlow.detail: Players with >7 cards discard half. Move the Robber OR the Pirate and steal 1 random card (Pirate: from a player with a ship on that hex).

turnFlow.title: Trade
turnFlow.detail: Bank 4:1, generic port 3:1, specific port 2:1, or trade resources with other players (no gifts).

turnFlow.title: Build
turnFlow.detail: Roads, ships, settlements, cities, dev cards — plus scenario pieces.

turnFlow.title: Move one ship (optional)
turnFlow.detail: Once per turn, move an open-end ship (not built this turn, not in a closed route) to any legal edge.

turnFlow.title: Pass
turnFlow.detail: Pass the dice to the player on your left.

beginner.title: Ships are movable roads
beginner.body: Build ships to cross water; once per turn you can re-route the open end of a chain. Lay them loosely, then aim at whichever island opponents leave open.

beginner.title: Ships cost wood + wool
beginner.body: Land roads are wood + brick, but every ship is 1 lumber + 1 wool. Pick a start with steady wool and wood so you can actually afford to sail.

beginner.title: Chase new-island bonuses
beginner.body: Most scenarios award bonus VP for your first settlement on each new island — often worth more than a hotter number back home.

beginner.title: Gold is a wild resource
beginner.body: Gold-field hexes pay out any resource you choose, so a gold spot is more flexible than its pip count looks. Treat it like a premium number.

intermediate.title: Pirate beats robber at sea
intermediate.body: On a 7, parking the pirate beside an opponent's ships freezes their sea expansion and still lets you steal — usually better than blocking a land hex.

intermediate.title: Longest Route counts ships too
intermediate.body: Longest Trade Route adds roads and ships together. When rivals wall off your land, a sea leg can win or hold the 2 VP.

intermediate.title: Make every ship pay
intermediate.body: An island settlement is several ships plus the build. Commit only when the new production or island bonus clearly earns those resources back.

advanced.title: Guard your route's open end
advanced.body: A single enemy ship at an ambiguous junction can cut your longest route from its anchor settlement, costing Longest Route and 2 VP. Leave no open ends in the final turns.

advanced.title: Win the landing race
advanced.body: First-settlement bonuses go to whoever arrives first. Against a rival eyeing the same island, an extra ship to land one turn early can swing a net VP.

advanced.title: Feed the ship engine
advanced.body: Sea expansion burns resources fast, so dead turns hurt more. Anchor on gold and 6/8 hexes for the wool and wood that keep a route moving.

cities-knights.name: Catan: Cities & Knights
cities-knights.description: A deeper strategic experience for people who thought base Catan was too relaxing. Commodities replace some resources (more things to fight over!), city improvements unlock powerful abilities (that your opponents will use against you), and the Barbarians threaten your cities every single turn — because you needed one more thing to worry about. Features 3 decks of progress cards, knights that constantly need feeding, and the joy of watching your undefended city get pillaged. 13 VP to win, infinite regret along the way and the gold standard of “it’s just a game.”

cards.name: Cloth
cards.description: Commodity produced by cities on Pasture hexes. Used to advance in the Trade column of city improvements.
usages: Produced by cities on Pasture hexes (doubled roll)
Invest in Trade city improvements

cards.name: Coin
cards.description: Commodity produced by upgraded Mountain cities. Used to advance in the Politics column.
usages: Produced by cities on Mountain hexes
Invest in Science city improvements

cards.name: Paper
cards.description: Commodity produced by upgraded Forest cities. Used to advance in the Science column.
usages: Produced by cities on Forest hexes
Invest in Politics city improvements

cards.name: Commercial Harbor
cards.description: Each opponent must choose a commodity card from their hand and give it to you in exchange for a resource card of your choice from your hand.
usages: Force advantageous trades with all opponents
Deplete opponents' commodity reserves

cards.name: Master Merchant (Guild Dues)
cards.description: Look at the hand cards of an opponent who has more victory points than you. Take 2 resource or commodity cards of your choice from that hand.
usages: Gain intelligence on an opponent's hand
Steal 2 specific cards from a neighbor

cards.name: Merchant
cards.description: Place the Merchant on any land hex adjacent to one of your settlements or cities. While you hold the Merchant, you trade that hex's resource at 2:1. Worth 1 VP.
usages: Gain a 2:1 trade ratio on a chosen resource
Worth 1 VP while you control the Merchant

cards.name: Merchant Fleet
cards.description: Select 1 type of resource or commodity. For the remainder of this turn, you may trade 2 of that type for any 1 other resource or commodity.
usages: Get a temporary 2:1 trade ratio on any type
Great when you have a surplus of one resource

cards.name: Resource Monopoly
cards.description: Name 1 resource type. Each opponent must give you 2 cards of that resource if they have them; a player with only 1 must give that 1.
usages: Collect up to 6 resources from 3 opponents
Weaker than base game Monopoly but still powerful

cards.name: Trade Monopoly
cards.description: Name 1 commodity type. Each opponent who has 1 or more of that commodity must give you exactly 1 of them.
usages: Collect commodities from all opponents at once
Disrupts opponents' city improvement plans

cards.name: Alchemist (Alchemy)
cards.description: Before rolling the dice on your turn, choose the result of the production dice (both numbers). The event die is still rolled normally.
usages: Guarantee production from your best hexes
Trigger a 7 to activate the robber strategically

cards.name: Crane
cards.description: This turn, you may build one city improvement for 1 fewer commodity than the normal cost.
usages: Save a commodity when upgrading a city track
Reach higher improvement levels faster

cards.name: Engineer (Engineering)
cards.description: Build 1 city wall for free (no resources required). Place it under one of your cities.
usages: Protect a city without spending resources
City walls add +2 to your hand limit when a 7 is rolled

cards.name: Inventor (Invention)
cards.description: Swap 2 number tokens on the board. You may not swap the tokens with the numbers 2, 6, 8, or 12.
usages: Improve production odds on your hexes
Weaken an opponent's hex by moving a good number away

cards.name: Irrigation
cards.description: Take 2 grain cards from the bank for each field hex adjacent to at least one of your buildings.
usages: Massive grain boost if well-positioned on fields
Great for fueling knight activations

cards.name: Medicine
cards.description: This turn, you may upgrade one settlement to a city at a reduced cost: only 2 Ore + 1 Grain (instead of 3 Ore + 2 Grain).
usages: Build a city at a fraction of the normal cost
Quickly expand your city network

cards.name: Mining
cards.description: Take 2 ore cards from the bank for each mountain hex adjacent to at least one of your buildings.
usages: Huge ore gain if you border multiple mountains
Fuel city upgrades and knight recruitment

cards.name: Printer (Printing)
cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. This card remains face-up in front of you for the rest of the game.
usages: Permanent 1 VP — play it immediately
Cannot be stolen or lost

cards.name: Road Building
cards.description: Place 2 roads on the board for free, as if you had just built them.
usages: Expand your network quickly
Compete for Longest Road (2 VP)

cards.name: Smith (Smithing)
cards.description: Promote up to 2 of your knights for free (e.g., Basic → Strong, or Strong → Mighty).
usages: Strengthen your defense without spending resources
Prepare for barbarian attacks efficiently

cards.name: Bishop (Taxation)
cards.description: Move the robber to a new hex. Steal 1 random card (resource or commodity) from each opponent with a building on the robber's new hex.
usages: Collect 1 resource from each affected opponent
Relocate the robber to disrupt multiple players

cards.name: Constitution
cards.description: Worth 1 Victory Point. This card remains face-up in front of you for the rest of the game.
usages: Permanent 1 VP — play it immediately
Cannot be stolen or lost

cards.name: Deserter (Treason)
cards.description: Choose another player; they must remove one of their knights from the board. You may then place one of your knights of equal or lower strength.
usages: Weaken an opponent's defense before a barbarian attack
Remove a knight blocking your road

cards.name: Diplomat (Diplomacy)
cards.description: Remove any open road (a road with at least one end not connected to another road, settlement, or city). If it is your own road, you may immediately place it elsewhere for free.
usages: Relocate one of your own roads strategically
Remove an opponent's road to break their Longest Road

cards.name: Intrigue
cards.description: Displace an opponent's knight without using one of your own knights. The target knight must be on an intersection connected to one of your routes; the opponent then moves it to a legal intersection or removes it.
usages: Clear a key intersection for your own use
Force an opponent's knight out of a strategic position

cards.name: Saboteur (Sabotage)
cards.description: Each opponent with equal or more victory points than you must discard half of their hand cards (rounded down).
usages: Punish the leading players
Effective when you are behind in VP

cards.name: Spy (Espionage)
cards.description: Look at an opponent's hand of progress cards and steal 1 of your choice.
usages: Gain intelligence and steal a powerful card
Disrupt an opponent's planned strategy

cards.name: Warlord (Encouragement)
cards.description: Activate all of your knights for free (without paying the usual grain cost).
usages: Instantly prepare all knights for barbarian defense
Save significant resources on activations

cards.name: Wedding
cards.description: Each opponent with more victory points than you must give you 2 resource or commodity cards of their choice.
usages: Gain cards from players who are ahead
Most effective when you are trailing in VP

cards.name: Trade (Cloth)
cards.description: You may trade commodities at a 2:1 ratio for any resource or other commodity.
usages: Requires level 3 on the Trade track
Commodity used: Cloth (from Pasture cities)
Level 4 earns the Trade Metropolis (2 VP)

cards.name: Politics (Coin)
cards.description: You may promote strong knights (level 2) to mighty knights (level 3).
usages: Requires level 3 on the Politics track
Commodity used: Coin (from Mountain cities)
Level 4 earns the Politics Metropolis (2 VP)

cards.name: Science (Paper)
cards.description: If you receive no cards during the Production phase, you may take 1 resource card of your choice (except when a 7 is rolled).
usages: Requires level 3 on the Science track
Commodity used: Paper (from Forest cities)
Level 4 earns the Science Metropolis (2 VP)

cards.name: Barbarian Attack
cards.description: Each turn a ship is rolled, the Barbarian token advances. When it reaches Catan, a battle is resolved. If barbarians win, the player with fewest knights loses a city.
usages: Build and activate Knights to defend
City Walls do NOT stop pillage; they only raise your 7-discard limit (+2 each)

setup: Uses the C&K sea frame with barbarian track.
No base game development cards — replaced by progress cards (3 decks).
No Largest Army tile.
Each player's second starting piece is a city (not a settlement).
Each player gets a city improvement board with 3 tracks and 3 cubes.
🥷 Robber starts off the board until the first barbarian attack.

turnOverview.title: 1. Roll Dice + Event Dice
turnOverview.detail: Production dice determines resources. Event dice advances barbarians or triggers progress card draws.

turnOverview.title: 2. Commodities
turnOverview.detail: Cities on mountains produce Coin (+Ore), on pastures produce Cloth (+Wool), on forests produce Paper (+Wood).

turnOverview.title: 3. Action Phase
turnOverview.detail: Trade, build, improve cities, recruit/activate knights, or play progress cards.

keyRules.title: Commodities
keyRules.detail: Cities produce commodities alongside resources: Coin (mountains), Cloth (pastures), Paper (forests). Used to advance city improvement tracks.

keyRules.title: City Improvements
keyRules.detail: 3 tracks — Trade, Science, Politics. Advance by spending commodities. Level 3 unlocks a permanent ability. Level 4 earns a Metropolis (2 VP).

keyRules.title: Metropolis
keyRules.detail: First to level 4 on a track gains that Metropolis (placed on a city, total 4 VP). First to level 5 gets permanent control. Cannot be pillaged.

keyRules.title: Knights
keyRules.detail: 3 strength levels: Basic, Strong, Mighty. Must be recruited then activated (costs 1 Grain). Can move, displace weaker enemy knights, or chase the robber. All deactivate after barbarian attack.

keyRules.title: Barbarian Attack
keyRules.detail: Barbarian strength = total cities on board. Defender strength = sum of active knights. If barbarians win: player(s) with the lowest total active-knight strength lose a city (downgraded to settlement). Metropolises are immune.

keyRules.title: City Walls
keyRules.detail: Placed under cities. Each wall adds +2 to your hand limit when a 7 is rolled. Max 3 walls.

keyRules.title: Progress Cards
keyRules.detail: Drawn based on event die + your track level. Hand limit of 4 progress cards. Many unique effects across 3 decks (Trade, Science, Politics).

keyRules.title: The Merchant
keyRules.detail: Placed via progress card on a hex adjacent to your building. Gives 2:1 trade on that resource and is worth 1 VP.

scenarios.name: Combining with Seafarers
scenarios.description: Play Cities & Knights on a Seafarers scenario map. Add 2 VP to that scenario's victory target.
details: Best fits: Heading for New Shores or Through the Desert (16 VP each). Avoid The Fog Islands and The Four Islands — they make the barbarians much tougher.
Barbarians attack all islands at once: cities and active knights on every island count.
Ships count as roads for all C&K rules. Knights can move along ship routes, stop on sea intersections and chase away the pirate from there.
Gold fields produce resources only, never commodities. The merchant can't be placed on a gold field.

scenarios.name: 5–6 Player Extension (5–6 Player Expansion)
scenarios.description: Adds a 5th and 6th player. Also needs the base game's 5–6 player set; all other C&K rules are unchanged.
details: Board: the larger 5–6 player island, with the C&K barbarian track alongside.
Special Build Phase after every turn: in clockwise order, each other player may build (incl. knights, city walls and city improvements) and activate or promote knights.
No trading, progress cards or knight actions in the Special Build Phase. A knight activated there can act on its owner's next turn.
2025 6th ed: paired turns replace the Special Build Phase — the player 3 seats to the active player's left also takes an Action phase, but may not trade with other players.

reference.tradingNote: C&K adds commodity trades via the Trade Progress deck and the Merchant token (2:1 on an adjacent hex). Commodities (coin / paper / cloth) also trade 4:1 at the bank.

turnFlow.title: Play a progress card (optional)
turnFlow.detail: Only the Alchemist (Alchemy) card may be played before rolling.

turnFlow.title: Roll production + event die
turnFlow.detail: Red + yellow production dice AND the colored event die (barbarian ship, or one of the three city-improvement icons: Trade, Science, Politics).

turnFlow.title: Production & commodities
turnFlow.detail: Settlements → 1 resource. Cities → 1 resource + 1 commodity from pasture/forest/mountain hexes.

turnFlow.title: Barbarian advance
turnFlow.detail: On a barbarian event die face, the barbarian ship advances. If it reaches Catan, a battle resolves: if knights are too weak, the lowest-strength defender(s) each lose a city (→ settlement); if knights are strong enough, the single strongest defender wins a Defender of Catan VP.

turnFlow.title: On a 7: Robber
turnFlow.detail: As base game. Knights on the board are unaffected.

turnFlow.title: Trade / Build / Activate knights
turnFlow.detail: Spend resources & commodities. Knights must be activated (1 Grain) before they can move/chase robber.

turnFlow.title: Pass
turnFlow.detail: End turn, hand dice to left.

beginner.title: Cities are your engine
beginner.body: Only cities make commodities (coin, cloth, paper), and almost every Cities & Knights card needs them. Aim for a second city by turn 5–6.

beginner.title: Match terrain to your track
beginner.body: Ore makes coin (Politics), wool makes cloth (Trade), wood makes paper (Science). Put cities on the commodity that feeds the track you want.

beginner.title: Be ready for the first barbarian attack
beginner.body: Build and activate a knight early — the barbarian ship lands sooner than new players expect, and when Catan falls the weakest defender loses a city.

beginner.title: Never lose your last city
beginner.body: This is the single most important thing in Cities & Knights. Lose your last city and your engine stalls: settlements make no commodities, so every improvement you bought sits useless until you rebuild. Guard it above all else.

beginner.title: Wall up before a 7 hurts
beginner.body: Each city wall lets you hold two more cards. As commodities pile up, walls stop a robber roll from gutting your hand.

intermediate.title: Focus one track, but touch all three
intermediate.body: Drive one track to level 3+, yet still grab cheap level-1 improvements on the other two. Every level you hold lets you draw that colour's progress card, so a little breadth keeps cards flowing while your main track wins.

intermediate.title: Level 3 is the real payoff
intermediate.body: Science 3 gives the Aqueduct (a free resource on dead rolls), Politics 3 unlocks mighty knights, Trade 3 brings better trade rates. Get your main track there fast.

intermediate.title: Promote knights, don't just stack them
intermediate.body: A mighty (level-3) knight brings 3 strength for the same one-grain activation, and outranks enemy knights when you displace them or chase the robber. Quality beats a crowd of basics.

advanced.title: Stack up Defender of Catan VPs
advanced.body: Each repelled attack, the single strongest defender takes a Defender of Catan victory point. There are several attacks per game, so being top knight again and again is a quiet path to multiple points.

advanced.title: Time the metropolis around barbarians
advanced.body: Track level 4 upgrades a city to a metropolis (+2 VP) that can never be pillaged. Lock it in when barbarians are 1–2 rolls from landing, so your VP is safe even if a city falls.

advanced.title: Build toward the swing cards
advanced.body: A few progress cards decide games: Printer and Constitution are kept victory points, Bishop loots a whole cluster, Alchemist sets the dice. Steer your track toward the deck that wins your game.

traders-barbarians.name: Catan: Traders & Barbarians
traders-barbarians.descriptionTitle: 🐫 Five Ways to Complicate a Perfectly Good Board Game
traders-barbarians.description: A collection of five scenarios and variants that add new dimensions to the classic game — because someone at Catan Studio looked at the base game and thought 'needs more camels.' Features trade routes where you deliver goods across the island like an unpaid intern, barbarian invasions that keep you on your toes, and enough variant rules to make your rulebook thicker than a phone book. Perfect for the group that's played base Catan 200 times and needs fresh reasons to argue.

cards.name: Caravan (Merchant Train)
cards.description: In The Caravans scenario (renamed 'Merchant Trains' in the 6th edition), camels — called wagons in the new edition — extend routes out from the central oasis (the 'watering hole'). Whenever a settlement is built or upgraded, players vote for the right to place the next camel; each vote costs 1 wheat or 1 wool.
usages: A settlement or city on a camel (wagon) route scores +1 extra VP
A camel route counts double toward the Longest Road (Longest Route)

cards.name: Gold Coin Token
cards.description: Gold coins, earned by delivering goods or by trading resources to the supply. Spend 2 gold to take any 1 resource from the supply — at most twice per turn. Gold is never a wild resource and is never worth victory points.
usages: Spend 2 gold for any 1 resource from the supply (max twice per turn)
Earn gold by delivering goods or trading resources to the supply

cards.name: Commodities
cards.description: Traders & Barbarians main scenario. Your wagon picks up one commodity at a time at the center of a trade hex (commodity hex) and hauls it to the hex that needs it.
usages: Quarry: needs tools — supplies sand and marble
Glassworks: needs sand — supplies glass and tools
Castle: needs marble and glass — supplies tools and sand
Each delivery = 1 VP plus 1–5 gold — more as you upgrade your baggage train (wagon)

cards.name: Knight
cards.description: Barbarian Attack scenario only. Knights enter play through this scenario's development cards and stand on hex edges, like roads. They free the coast by outnumbering the barbarians on a hex.
usages: End of turn: move each knight up to 3 edges — pay 1 grain to move that knight up to 5
Victory when a hex's edges hold more knights than there are barbarians on it — the barbarians become prisoners
Every 2 prisoners = 1 VP; an involved player left without a prisoner takes 3 gold
After each victory a die roll sends some knights home — 3 gold for each knight lost

setup: Modular expansion — 4 standalone variants and 5 standalone scenarios.
Variants and scenarios can be mixed and matched.
Includes a 2-player variant with neutral players.

keyRules.title: Modular Design
keyRules.detail: Each variant/scenario adds or changes specific rules. Pick and combine freely with the base game.

scenarios.name: The Friendly Robber
scenarios.description: The Robber cannot be moved to a hex with a building of a player who only has 2 VP.
details: Protects beginners from early-game targeting

scenarios.name: The Harbor Master (Strongest Ports / Harbors of Catan)
scenarios.description: Strongest Ports tile (2 VP) for the player with most VP in buildings on ports.
details: Encourages port building strategy

scenarios.name: CATAN Event Cards
scenarios.description: 37-card event deck replaces dice rolls.
details: Cards have production numbers + special events
Events include Earthquake, Epidemic, Good Neighbors
New Year card triggers deck reshuffle

scenarios.name: CATAN for Two
scenarios.description: 2-player variant with neutral players.
details: Double production phase (roll twice)
Trade tokens for forced trades or moving the robber
Must build for neutral players when you build

scenarios.name: The Fishermen of Catan (Fishing on Catan)
scenarios.description: Lake hex replaces desert with fishing grounds on coasts.
details: Fish tokens earned from production
Spend fish: remove robber (2), steal card (3), free resource (4), free road (5), free dev card (7)
Old boot = need +1 VP to win

scenarios.name: Rivers of Catan
scenarios.description: River tiles replace 7 hexes. Bridges cross rivers.
details: Bridge cost: 2 Brick + 1 Wood
Gold coins from river tiles
Wealthiest Catanian (1 VP) / Poorest (-2 VP)

scenarios.name: The Caravans (Merchant Trains)
scenarios.description: Camels (wagons in the 6th-edition 'Merchant Trains') form routes out from the central oasis (watering hole).
details: Vote to place a camel whenever a settlement is built or upgraded (pay 1 wheat or 1 wool)
A settlement or city on a camel route = +1 VP
Camel routes count double for the Longest Road (Longest Route)

scenarios.name: Barbarian Attack
scenarios.description: Castle hex on board. Knights defend against barbarian landings.
details: No robber or base development cards
Knights placed on hex edges
3 barbarians conquer a hex; prisoners = VP

scenarios.name: Traders & Barbarians (main scenario)
scenarios.description: 3 commodity hexes. Wagons transport goods between them.
details: Wagon upgrades increase movement
Gold earned from deliveries
Barbarians block roads

reference.tradingNote: T&B introduces caravans, trade routes and gold — some scenarios replace the standard bank trade with delivery-based VP. Always check the specific scenario rules before assuming 4:1 still applies.

trading.title: Caravans (scenario)
trading.detail: Move caravans up to 3 road segments per turn; deliver goods tokens to the friendly village for a VP.

trading.title: Gold (scenario)
trading.detail: Trade gold tokens earned from rivers or trade routes at 2:1 at the bank.

strategy.subheading: Traders & Barbarians is a toolbox of scenarios and variants — open the one you're playing.

groups.name: The Fishermen of Catan (Fishing on Catan)

tips.title: Fish are free insurance
tips.body: Lakes give fish tokens, not resources. A spot by the lake lets you turn fish into the exact resource you're short on, quietly smoothing out bad rolls.

tips.title: Spend fish, don't hoard
tips.body: Fish cash in (in the printed combos) to draw a resource from the bank, swipe a card, or shove the robber. Steady small spends keep your plan moving; a giant pile is wasted tempo.

tips.title: Fish let you play small-handed
tips.body: Since fish fetch what you need on demand, keep your hand under the robber limit and convert only at the moment you build.

tips.title: Gold is a 2:1 voucher
tips.body: River gold isn't built with directly; two gold buys any one resource, any time. A flexible wild that's never the wrong card.

tips.title: Convert gold as you build
tips.body: Don't sit on a pile; cash it the turn you build. Gold also hides your plan — opponents can't read what you'll make from it.

tips.title: Bridge for an unblockable road
tips.body: A bridge crosses a river section no one else can. One in the right gap claims or extends Longest Road where rivals can't cut you — a quiet 2 VP swing.

tips.title: Build where the routes will run
tips.body: You score by having camels (wagons) pass through your own settlements and cities — a building on a camel route is worth +1 VP. Place your early buildings where routes from the oasis can naturally reach them.

tips.title: Win the placement votes
tips.body: Every time anyone builds or upgrades a settlement there's a vote to place the next camel (1 wheat or 1 wool). Spend to steer routes through your own buildings — and away from rivals' — because those votes are how you actually score.

tips.title: Double-dip with Longest Road
tips.body: A camel (wagon) route counts double toward the Longest Road (Longest Route). Plan routes that also serve as your road network so the same camels score your buildings and hand you the 2-VP bonus.

tips.title: Have a knight before they land
tips.body: Barbarians strike the coast, and an undefended coastal building can be conquered — it stops scoring VP until you liberate it with knights, but it is not destroyed. Build at least one knight before the army arrives.

tips.title: Defend a turn ahead
tips.body: Watch the barbarians' advance and have knights in place one turn before they hit, covering your most valuable coastal spots. Reacting after the landing is usually too late.

tips.title: Triage the coastline
tips.body: When you can't cover everything, let the cheapest corner fall and mass knights on your cities and key production. Bake the barbarians' pace into your build order so you're never caught flat.

tips.title: Roads are delivery routes
tips.body: Your roads carry trade goods to the castle, not just chase Longest Road. Aim your first roads at the goods and the castle so deliveries start early.

tips.title: Run the routes that pay most
tips.body: Favor short, high-value deliveries, and lay one road spine that serves several pickups. Delivery income is reliable — it doesn't depend on the dice the way production does.

tips.title: Balance hauling vs. the VP race
tips.body: Don't tunnel on deliveries while a rival closes on the win. Keep an eye on barbarian defense and points, and convert your delivery income into VP at the moment it matters.

groups.name: The Harbor Master (Strongest Ports / Harbors of Catan)

tips.title: Cities on harbors score double
tips.body: A harbor settlement is 1 point and a harbor city is 2 toward the +2 VP Harbor Master card. Upgrading your harbor spots is the cheapest path to it.

tips.title: Lead by the minimum
tips.body: Harbor Master works like Largest Army — you only need to be ahead. Claim it with the fewest points spent and reinforce only when someone actually threatens it.

tips.title: Flip it at the buzzer
tips.body: It can change hands on the last turn. Keep a coastal city upgrade ready to steal the 2 VP when it counts, and track whether a rival is one point from taking it from you.

tips.title: You're safe at 2 VP or fewer
tips.body: The robber can't sit on you and no one can steal from you while you're on 2 VP or fewer. Expand freely early — your start is protected.

tips.title: The robber chases the leaders
tips.body: Once you pull ahead you become the only legal target, so expect the robber and 7s to land on you. Keep your hand lean and your production spread so one blocked hex doesn't sink you.

tips.title: Time when you cross 2 VP
tips.body: Jumping from 2 to 3 VP drops your immunity. Occasionally it's worth holding at 2 a little longer to keep producing safely, then surging once your engine is set.

tips.title: Numbers come from a deck
tips.body: The dice are replaced by a card deck, so over a full pass every number shows up its fair share. The luck still evens out — it just does so on a schedule.

tips.title: Count what's been played
tips.body: A number that's already shown all its copies can't return until the reshuffle. Favor placements on numbers that are still 'due' and lean away from ones that are spent.

tips.title: Track the 7s and the reshuffle
tips.body: Sevens arrive on a known cadence, so drop your hand under the limit as one nears. Right after the dangerous cards are spent is the safest window to carry resources and make big builds.

explorers-pirates.name: Catan: Explorers & Pirates
explorers-pirates.descriptionTitle: 🏴‍☠️ Catan Goes Full Columbus (Minus the Controversy)
explorers-pirates.description: Set sail to explore unknown waters because sitting on a known island was getting boring. Build ships and harbors, complete missions like spice trade or fish hauls (yes, fish — peak adventure), and colonize new lands far from home. Think of it as Seafarers' ambitious older sibling who studied abroad and won't stop talking about it. More moving pieces, more missions, more 'wait, whose turn is it?' moments.

cards.name: Spice Haul
cards.description: Sail your ship to a distant spice island and deliver the spice sack to the Council of Catan for Victory Points.
usages: Each completed haul earns 1 VP
Requires reaching and returning from the spice tile

cards.name: Fish Camp
cards.description: Catch fish hauls at fish shoals (once per Movement phase roll a die matching an explored shoal), then sail them to the Council of Catan.
usages: Deliver fish hauls to the Council of Catan to advance the fish mission track
Position near coastal hexes with good numbers

cards.name: Pirate Lair
cards.description: Discover and destroy pirate lairs scattered across the frontier. Each cleared lair earns 1 Victory Point.
usages: Unload crew onto the gold field — the lair is captured by the 3rd crew
Capturing advances your pirate mission track — it does not score on discovery

cards.name: Council of Catan
cards.description: Island stronghold just off the starting island (it counts as a sea hex). Deliver fish hauls and spice sacks at its anchor docks.
usages: Unload when either end of your ship touches an anchor
Each fish haul delivered → +1 step on the fish track
Each spice sack delivered → +1 step on the spice track
No pirate ship may be placed on it

cards.name: Fish Haul
cards.description: Large cargo piece (6 in the supply). Catch it at a fish shoal and deliver it to the Council of Catan.
usages: Catch: an empty ship with an end next to a shoal holding a haul loads it
Fills the whole hold — 1 per ship or harbor settlement
Deliver at a Council anchor → +1 step on the fish track (haul returns to the supply)
A pirate ship placed on a shoal removes its haul

cards.name: Spice Sack
cards.description: Small cargo piece. Load one by dropping a crew on a spice hex, then deliver it to the Council of Catan.
usages: Drop 1 crew on a spice hex → load 1 spice sack straight away
Only 1 sack per player from each spice hex
Small piece: 2 fit in a ship or harbor settlement
Deliver at a Council anchor → +1 step on the spice track per sack

cards.name: Spice Hex (Spice Farm)
cards.description: Village hex found while exploring. Put 1 crew on it (the crew stays for good) to load a spice sack and gain its permanent ability.
usages: On discovery: take 2 gold and place 1 spice sack per player on it
Swift Voyage: all your ships get +1 MP (both Swift Voyage hexes: +2)
Pirate Bonus: you chase the pirate on a 6 or the hex's number (both: 4, 5 or 6)
Fast Gold: once per turn, sell 1 resource for 1 gold (both: twice)
No roads or settlements on it until you have placed a crew there

cards.name: Harbor Settlement
cards.description: Upgrade of one of your coastal settlements, worth 2 VP. Home port for your new ships, settlers and crews.
usages: Cost: 2 Grain + 2 Ore — replaces a coastal settlement (max 4 per player)
Collects 1 resource like a settlement (not 2 like a city)
New ships are built next to it; new settlers and crews go in it or an adjacent ship
Holds 1 large piece (settler, fish haul) or 2 small pieces (crews, spice sacks)

cards.name: Ship
cards.description: Carries your cargo across the sea. Unlike Seafarers ships, which form routes like roads, E&P ships sail freely using movement points.
usages: Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Wool — build next to one of your harbor settlements
4 movement points per turn; pay 1 Wool for +2 (once per ship per turn)
Holds 1 large piece (settler, fish haul) or 2 small pieces (crews, spice sacks)
Up to 2 ships per sea edge; discovering a hex ends that ship's move
3 ships per player — with none left, remove one (its cargo is lost) to build a new one

cards.name: Settler
cards.description: Large cargo piece (2 per player). Ship it to new land and swap it for a settlement.
usages: Cost: 1 Brick + 1 Lumber + 1 Wool + 1 Grain (same as a settlement)
Placed in your harbor settlement or an adjacent ship — never on land
Ship end next to a land intersection → return ship + settler, place a free settlement
Distance rule applies; no building on intersections touching an unexplored hex

cards.name: Crew
cards.description: Small cargo piece — your warriors and merchants for pirate lairs and spice hexes.
usages: Cost: 1 Wool + 1 Ore
Placed in your harbor settlement or an adjacent ship; 2 fit in either
Pirate lair: the 3rd crew on it (any mix of players) captures it
Spice hex: 1 crew per player, and it stays there → load 1 spice sack

cards.name: Pirate Ship
cards.description: Each player owns one, but only one is on the board at a time. It targets ships, not settlements.
usages: On your 7: place or move your pirate ship (an opponent's goes back to its owner)
Steal 1 random resource from one player with a ship on that hex (1 gold if they have no cards)
Tribute: 1 gold per ship moved onto, along or off its hex (its owner pays nothing)
Never on a sea hex next to the starting island, nor on the outer frame
Chase: each unmoved ship beside its hex rolls 1 die — a 6 drives it off and you place yours

cards.name: Gold Coin
cards.description: Universal currency in E&P. Each player starts with 2 gold; extras are awarded for no-production turns and exploration.
usages: 2 gold → 1 resource of your choice (max twice per turn)
3 identical resources → 1 gold at the supply
A production roll (not a 7) gives you nothing → take 1 gold
Discover a hex with no resource (sea, gold field, fish shoal, spice hex) → 2 gold
Tribute: 1 gold per ship moved onto, along or off an opponent's pirate hex

setup: Major departure from base game: no development cards, no cities, no robber.
Board has a starting island + 2 unexplored regions (facedown hexes).
First piece is a harbor settlement (on coast, worth 2 VP); second is a regular settlement.
Each player starts with 2 gold coins.
Trade with supply at 3:1 (no ports). Trade 2 gold for 1 resource (twice per turn).

turnOverview.title: 1. Production
turnOverview.detail: Roll dice for resources. Players with no production receive 1 gold instead.

turnOverview.title: 2. Trade & Build
turnOverview.detail: Trade, build settlements/ships, recruit settlers and crews.

turnOverview.title: 3. Ship Movement
turnOverview.detail: Each ship has 4 movement points. Pay 1 Wool for +2 MP. Ships carry settlers, crews, spice sacks, and fish hauls.

keyRules.title: Harbor Settlements
keyRules.detail: Worth 2 VP. Upgrade one of your coastal settlements for 2 Grain + 2 Ore (max 4). Can hold 1 large piece or 2 small pieces. Ships must be built adjacent.

keyRules.title: Ships
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Wool + 1 Lumber. Have 4 MP per turn. Carry pieces to destinations. Up to 2 ships per edge.

keyRules.title: Exploring
keyRules.detail: Moving a ship adjacent to a facedown hex flips it. Land hexes get a number disc. Gain 1 matching resource (or 2 gold) on discovery.

keyRules.title: Settlers
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Brick + 1 Lumber + 1 Wool + 1 Grain (same as a settlement). Carried on ships. Build a settlement by unloading at a land hex intersection.

keyRules.title: Crews
keyRules.detail: Cost: 1 Wool + 1 Ore. Used for pirate lair captures and spice farm activation.

keyRules.title: Pirate Ship
keyRules.detail: On a 7, place your pirate ship on a sea hex. Steal 1 resource from a player with a ship there. Moving past costs 1 gold tribute.

keyRules.title: Chase Away Pirate
keyRules.detail: Unmoved ship adjacent to pirate hex rolls 1 die; a 6 chases the pirate away.

keyRules.title: Missions
keyRules.detail: Taking part in a lair capture, or delivering a fish haul or spice sack, moves your marker 1 space (a lair's hero moves 1 more); you score the VP symbols shown next to it. The player furthest along a track holds its VP card (bonus VP tile, +1 VP); on a tie, the marker that arrived first keeps it.

scenarios.name: Land Ho!
scenarios.description: Learn exploration basics.
details: Discover hexes, build settlements on new islands
No crews, missions or pirate ships yet — a 7 only forces discards

scenarios.name: Pirate Lairs
scenarios.description: Capture pirate lairs on gold field hexes.
details: Place 3 crew to capture a lair
Hero (highest die + crew) advances extra on mission track
Furthest along the track holds the Greatest Pirate Scourge VP card (bonus VP tile): +1 VP

scenarios.name: Fish for Catan
scenarios.description: Catch and deliver fish to the Council of Catan.
details: Roll die during movement; matching fish shoal = fish haul
Deliver to Council to advance mission track

scenarios.name: Spices for Catan
scenarios.description: Deliver spice sacks to the Council.
details: Unload crew on spice farm, load spice sack, deliver
Each farm grants a permanent bonus (Swift Voyage, Pirate Bonus, Fast Gold)

scenarios.name: Explorers & Pirates (Full)
scenarios.description: The complete experience with all 3 missions.
details: All missions active simultaneously
Mission track positions and bonus VP tiles contribute to victory

buildingCosts.name: Road
buildingCosts.note: Only on explored land. No Longest Road (Longest Route) card in E&P.

buildingCosts.name: Settlement
buildingCosts.note: Build along your road, or place one free by landing a settler. Distance rule applies.

buildingCosts.name: Harbor Settlement
buildingCosts.note: Replaces one of your coastal settlements. Collects 1 resource. Max 4 per player.

buildingCosts.name: Ship
buildingCosts.note: Build next to your harbor settlement. 4 MP per turn. Max 2 per edge, 3 per player.

buildingCosts.name: Extra Ship Move
buildingCosts.note: +2 MP for one ship. Once per ship per turn.

buildingCosts.name: Settler
buildingCosts.note: Placed in a harbor settlement or adjacent ship. Land it to place a free settlement.

buildingCosts.name: Crew
buildingCosts.note: Captures pirate lairs and works spice hexes.

trading.title: Supply
trading.detail: 3 identical resources → 1 other resource or 1 gold, during your trade & build phase (Action phase). No ports in E&P.

trading.title: Gold Coin
trading.detail: Spend 2 gold for any 1 resource. Max twice per turn.

trading.title: Player Trade
trading.detail: Trade resources and gold with other players during your trade & build phase.

reference.tradingNote: E&P uses a 3:1 bank rate with no ports (or 2 gold for any 1 resource, twice per turn) and adds mission-driven trades (fish for Council VPs, spice sacks for mission progress). Treat mission rewards as better than any bank trade when feasible.

turnFlow.title: Roll & produce
turnFlow.detail: Settlements and harbor settlements collect 1 resource each; captured gold fields pay 2 gold per building. Got nothing (not on a 7)? Take 1 gold.

turnFlow.title: On a 7: pirate ship
turnFlow.detail: Players with more than 7 resource cards discard half. Place or move your pirate ship, then steal 1 random resource from one player with a ship on that hex (no pirate in Land Ho!).

turnFlow.title: Trade
turnFlow.detail: With players (resources and gold), the supply at 3:1 (for a resource or 1 gold), or 2 gold → 1 resource (twice per turn).

turnFlow.title: Build
turnFlow.detail: Roads, settlements, harbor settlements, ships, settlers and crews, mixed freely with trading. No cities, no development cards.

turnFlow.title: Move ships
turnFlow.detail: 4 MP each (+2 for 1 wool). Explore, load/unload, pay tribute, chase the pirate, catch fish, land settlers and crews, deliver to the Council. No trading or building now, except settling with a settler.

turnFlow.title: Resolve & pass
turnFlow.detail: Resolve any pirate lair captured this turn, then pass the dice. Reach the scenario's VP target (17 in the full game) on your turn and you win at once.

beginner.title: Open with your harbor settlement
beginner.body: Your first piece is a harbor settlement (2 VP) on the coast, and ships can only be built next to harbor settlements. Pick a coast that opens good sea lanes — it's your launchpad for everything.

beginner.title: Ships are your roads
beginner.body: There are no land roads here. Ships (1 wool + 1 lumber, 4 movement) carry settlers, crews, fish and spices across the sea — keep a small fleet moving every turn.

beginner.title: Explore for free rewards
beginner.body: Move a ship next to a face-down hex to flip it: you gain 1 matching resource (or 2 gold) for the discovery. Early exploration is free income and opens new land to settle.

beginner.title: No production? Take the gold
beginner.body: With no dev cards or cities, gold is your safety net — a dead production turn gives you 1 gold, and 2 gold buys any resource (twice per turn). Lean on it to keep building.

intermediate.title: Settle the islands you discover
intermediate.body: Settlers (1 brick + 1 lumber + 1 wool + 1 grain) ride a ship and drop on a new land intersection. Fresh islands mean new production and more harbor spots — expansion by sea is how you grow.

intermediate.title: Commit to two missions, not three
intermediate.body: Fish, spices and pirate lairs all advance the mission track, but chasing all three keeps you middling everywhere. Pick the two your board supports and push them hard.

intermediate.title: Load crews, not just settlers
intermediate.body: Crews (1 wool + 1 ore) are the mission workhorses: they capture pirate lairs, activate spice farms and bring in fish. A ship carrying a crew does work a settler can't.

intermediate.title: Deliver to the Council fast
intermediate.body: Fish and spice missions only score when cargo reaches the Council. Plan the round trip — a short delivery loop beats a richer source you can't reach in time; pay 1 wool for +2 movement when a deadline is tight.

advanced.title: Chase the spice-farm bonuses
advanced.body: Each spice farm you activate grants a permanent perk — Swift Voyage, Pirate Bonus or Fast Gold. Grab the one that compounds your plan early; it pays off all game.

advanced.title: Win the hero race at pirate lairs
advanced.body: Capturing a lair takes 3 crew, and the hero (highest die + crew) advances extra on the mission track. Arrive with a full crew and the dice edge — or block a rival's lair with one crew to buy yourself a turn.

advanced.title: Respect the pirate ship
advanced.body: On a 7 the pirate parks on a sea hex, robs ships there, and charges 1 gold tribute to sail past. Keep an unmoved ship beside it for a 6-to-chase, and route cargo around it near the endgame.

advanced.title: Race to 17, bank the cheap points
advanced.body: Victory comes from harbor settlements, settlements, mission-track positions and bonus VP tiles. Late game, take the cheapest point available — a harbor settlement or one mission step often beats a far-flung new island.
